idiom_name: axum Router + tower Layer middleware stack
implementation_notes: In axum the front controller is a value: Router::new().route(...) builds the dispatch table, .layer(...) applies tower Layers as the shared chain, and the result implements tower::Service, which axum::serve or hyper drives. What replaces the classic structure: one composed Service replaces the FrontController class, extractors (Path, State, TypedHeader) replace the request context and handler arguments, and middleware written with middleware::from_fn covers the common case without implementing Service by hand. Layers only wrap routes that were registered before them.
pitfalls: Router::layer only wraps routes already added and executes bottom-to-top, while ServiceBuilder runs top-to-bottom: mixing the two conventions yields a pipeline in the wrong order.
Layer type errors surface as enormous generic-bound messages; boxing with ServiceBuilder and adding HandleErrorLayer for fallible middleware keeps them tractable.
Blocking work inside an async handler blocks a runtime worker thread - use spawn_blocking - and a middleware that consumed the body cannot pass it on.
Services are cloned per request, so shared state must be cheap to clone behind an Arc, with mutation behind locks or channels rather than in the layer itself.
